body:
## Thesis

The stack-managed `AGENTS.md` contract block installed into a **consumer** repository commands every agent to read a set of entrypoint and control-plane files that the installer never places in that tree, and that no gate in the consumer tree can detect as missing. Two symptoms, one root cause: the contract text describes the factory's own dogfood environment, not the environment it installs.

## Symptom 1 — mandatory entrypoint is unsatisfiable in a consumer tree

`AGENTS.md` (inside the `ADAPTIVE-GROK-PRO:START/END` markers, i.e. machine-managed) states:

- "Fresh-clone bootstrap — `START_HERE.md` is the zero-context entrypoint. `PROJECT_STATE.json` is the machine-readable current handoff. A new agent must not require chat history…"
- "Mandatory entrypoint — For every software-development task: 1. Read `START_HERE.md`, `PROJECT_STATE.json`, and this contract."

Measured in the consumer tree (see `01-consumer-absence.txt`): every one of `START_HERE.md` (named on 3 lines, including "Mandatory entrypoint" step 1), `PROJECT_STATE.json` (5 lines), `mistakes.md` (2 lines), `VERSION` (1 line — "current VERSION" in the README-before-push rule), `architecture/` (1 line — `system.yaml`, `rules.yaml`, `generated/`) and `trust-ci/` (4 lines) is **absent**, and `git ls-files` returns **0** tracked paths for them. The same names all exist in the factory repository root itself (see `02-factory-root.txt`, fetched from `gh api .../git/trees/main`), which is why the prose reads correctly at home and breaks on install.

Consequence observed in practice: a session resuming after an interrupted run in that consumer repo had to reconstruct milestone, route, HEAD, receipts state and open findings from `git log`, `engineering/changes/*/state.json` and `.grok-stack/runtime/*` — exactly the reconstruction the entrypoint files exist to prevent.

## Symptom 2 — protected paths that do not exist

`.grok-stack/config/policy.json` lists `AGENTS.md`, `VERSION`, `mistakes.md`, `trust-ci/**`, `scripts/install_into.py` and `scripts/package_stack.py` among `control_plane_paths` (lines 21 and 64; same list in `adaptive_grok/_policy_legacy.py:22`). In the consumer tree only `AGENTS.md` is present of those — `managed.json` ships just the 13 `grok_*.py` entry points, so the two installer scripts the policy protects are not part of the payload at all. A protected-path grant can therefore name a file that has no bytes behind it, and `grok_verify`'s `architecture` / `governance` checks report `SKIP … not configured` (see `03-verify-gate.txt`), so nothing in the gate distinguishes "not configured" from "the contract says this file is required and it is gone".

## Related asymmetry

`managed.json` advertises the hook set (`UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `Stop`, …) and the contract says "The `UserPromptSubmit` hook classifies development tasks and writes `.grok-stack/runtime/active-route.json`. That route is the authority for local skills, agents, quality profiles, human gates". The hook payload is wired through `.grok/hooks.json` plus repo-root shims only; there is no registration for the agent CLI actually driving the session in that tree, and `active-route.json` was not touched by live prompts in a later session (its mtime predates them). Route-selected agents (`code_reviewer`, `test_reviewer`, …) are shipped only as `.grok/agents/*.md` and are not spawnable there, so the contract's "use only agents listed in `allowed_agents`" rule cannot be honoured literally and the review wave degrades to a generic agent briefed from the role file. Stated as observation, not as a claim about intended CLI coverage.

## What this is not

Not a product defect and not a Trust CI trust-boundary problem: no merge authority is involved. It is the installed agent contract asserting facts about a tree the installer does not produce.

## Evidence files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `01-consumer-absence.txt` | `test -e` matrix + `git ls-files` count for the named paths in the consumer tree, with the `ADAPTIVE-GROK-PRO` marker line numbers |
| `02-factory-root.txt` | factory repo root tree (same names present) via `gh api .../git/trees/main` |
| `03-verify-gate.txt` | `grok_verify --mode pr` check list showing `architecture`/`governance` = SKIP-not-configured next to a PASS verdict |
| `04-managed-and-policy.txt` | `managed.json` hook/agent/script inventory and `policy.json` `control_plane_paths` excerpt |

## Suggested direction (not a demand)

Either ship the entrypoint set with the install (templated `START_HERE.md` + `PROJECT_STATE.json` bound to the change package, plus a `mistakes.md` seed), or make the installed contract emit a consumer-scoped variant that references only what the installer writes — and make `grok_doctor` fail when a contract-named required path is absent, so the mismatch is detected by the gate instead of by the next resumed agent.

---

Evidence bundle (secret gist): <https://gist.github.com/Dimkox/1372c23ea1b998884d31320afb4a5f46>
Raw: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Dimkox/1372c23ea1b998884d31320afb4a5f46/raw/01-consumer-absence.txt>

## Erratum (self-correction, same day)

The first version of this body attributed `scripts/install_into.py` to `AGENTS.md`. Measured: `AGENTS.md` contains 0 occurrences of that name — it is a `policy.json` protected path (symptom 2), and the same is true of `scripts/package_stack.py`. `VERSION` does remain an `AGENTS.md` reference (1 line). Evidence file `01-consumer-absence.txt` was regenerated with explicit per-file "named in AGENTS.md / named in policy.json / exists at HEAD" columns so the attribution cannot be blurred again.
title: Installed AGENTS.md commands reading entrypoint files the installer never ships into a consumer tree

body:
## Summary

A consumer that vendors the `factory/` snapshot inherits `factory/README.md`, whose links point at files that live at the **stack repository root**, not inside the vendored subtree. In the consumer checkout those targets are never installed, so every one of them is a dead relative link. It makes a consumer-side markdown link audit permanently red and pushes teams into whitelisting the vendored tree, which then hides real breakage.

## Reproduction (read-only)

From a consumer repository that contains the vendored `factory/` tree:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('factory/README.md')
pat = re.compile(r'\]\((?!https?:|#|mailto:)([^)\s]+)')
for i, line in enumerate(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines(), 1):
    for m in pat.finditer(line):
        t = m.group(1).split('#')[0]
        if t and not (p.parent / t).resolve().exists():
            print(f'{i}: {m.group(1)}')
PY
```

Observed: 7 dead links, all `../`-escaped out of the vendored subtree — five into
`../engineering/runbooks/*.md`, one to `../DARK_FACTORY_ROADMAP.md`, one repeated.

Validated the checker itself with a control file containing one broken and one good relative
link: it reported exactly the broken one, and the same sweep over all tracked `*.md` outside
`factory/` returned 0 dead links. So this is the vendored README, not the audit.

## Why it happens

`install_into.py` scopes installation by `MANAGED_DIRS` / `MANAGED_FILES`, and `factory/` is
copied as a subtree of the stack tree. A subtree copy keeps intra-repo links that only resolve in
the original layout. The installer has no notion of "this file's relative links assume a parent
root", so nothing rewrites or flags them.

## Options (any one is fine)

1. Exclude `factory/README.md` from the copied set and let the consumer reference the stack
   repository instead — cheapest, and keeps the vendored tree honest about being a subtree.
2. Keep the README and rewrite root-escaping links to a stack-repository URL at install time, so
   they resolve outside the consumer.
3. Ship the referenced runbooks into the snapshot too — most complete, largest diff, and they are
   operator documents rather than consumer documentation.

## Impact

Cosmetic for runtime, non-cosmetic for verification hygiene: consumer repos commonly run a
relative-link check as part of a documentation gate, and this finding has to be suppressed there.
A `kept_local`-style declaration or a documented exemption list for the vendored subtree would
avoid each consumer inventing its own whitelist.
title: Vendored factory/ README ships 7 relative links that cannot resolve in a consumer tree
